records.title: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025)

records.title: Regulations Amending the Citizenship Regulations (Administrative Penalties and Consequences)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Citizenship Regulations (Administrative Penalties and Consequences) in order to (1) establish a new system of administrative penalties and consequences to address unauthorized practice and misrepresentation in immigration and citizenship services; (2) give Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada officers authority to investigate suspected violations, issue preliminary notices and notices of violations, and impose monetary penalties and consequences on individuals who engage in unauthorized practice or who misrepresent in immigration or citizenship services; and (3) require for the system to introduce clear penalties, a review process, and public disclosure of violators.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Administrative Penalties and Consequences)

records.title: Rules Amending the Refugee Protection Division Rules

records.title: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Asylum System Reform)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Asylum System Reform) in order to (1) reduce duplication by simplifying the online application process; (2) establish a time limit for Minister’s due diligence activities; (3) prescribe requirements regarding abandonment of claims /reinstatement of withdrawn claims; (4) set when designated representatives must be appointed; (5) provide quicker access to work permits for asylum seekers; and (6) create two exceptions to the new ineligibility provisions.

records.summary: Order fixing November 1, 2026 as the day on which certain provisions of the Contraventions Act comes into force in order to repeal stand-alone ticketing regimes found in various other federal statutes.

records.title: Order Acknowledging Receipt of the Assessment Done Under Subsection 23(1) of the Species at Risk Act (Basking Shark Atlantic Population and 14 Other Wildlife Species)
records.summary: Order Acknowledging Receipt of the Assessments done by the Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada (COSEWIC) with respect to the status of 15 aquatic species (Basking Shark Atlantic Population and 14 Other Wildlife Species).

records.title: Bedford Sherrard Remission Order
records.statute: Financial Administration Act Income Tax Act
records.summary: Bedford Sherrard Remission Order in order to remit $7,357.10 representing goods and services tax/harmonized sales tax (GST/HST), plus related interest, to Bedford Sherrard.

records.title: Remission Order in Respect of Canadian Dental Care Plan Eligibility Issues
records.summary: Remission Order in Respect of Canadian Dental Care Plan Eligibility Issues in order to remit costs equivalent to payments made to oral health providers by the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) for oral health services that were received by certain persons who incorrectly attested to not having access to dental insurance or coverage to enroll in the CDCP in the first three benefit periods (2024-2025, 2025-2026 and 2026-2027).

records.title: Regulations Amending the Employment Insurance Regulations (Pilot Project No. 25)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Employment Insurance Regulations (Pilot Project No. 25) in order to (1) waive the one-week waiting period until October 9, 2027; (2) suspend the treatment of monies paid on separation until October 9, 2027; (3) provide an additional 20 weeks of income support to long-tenured workers which applies to claims whose benefit period begins on or after October 11, 2026, but no later than June 12, 2027; and (4) simplify the treatment of rules on reasons for separation for claims whose benefit period begins on or after October 11, 2026, but no later than October 9, 2027.

records.title: High Risk Child Sex Offender Database Regulations
records.statute: High Risk Child Sex Offender Database Act
records.summary: High Risk Child Sex Offender Database Regulations in order to (1) require that the Commissioner review the information in the database by December 31 of the calendar year in which the regulations come into force, and then at least once every calendar year; and (2) establish 30 days as the period within which, if a decision is not made for the purposes of an application to remove information from the database, the Commissioner is deemed to have decided not to remove the information.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Queen's Regulations and Orders for the Canadian Forces
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Queen's Regulations and Orders for the Canadian Forces in order to add a new provision of the Act regarding an offence for the benefit of a criminal organization to the factors the military judge presiding at a court martial considers when determining the sentence.

records.title: Order Amending Schedule 1 to the Species at Risk Act (Canada Warbler and Six Other Wildlife Species)

records.title: Order Acknowledging Receipt of the Assessments Done Under Subsection 23(1) of the Species at Risk Act (Canada Warbler and Six Other Wildlife Species)

records.title: Regulations Amending the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985 in order to (1) update the regulations by removing references and representations of the obsolete LFA 37 area and divide the area equitably between LFA 36 and LFA 38 along the same interim boundaries that have been in place through conditions of licence since the 2022-23 fishing season.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Nuclear Liability and Compensation Act and the Nuclear Liability and Compensation Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Nuclear Liability and Compensation Act and the Nuclear Liability and Compensation Regulations in order to (1) increase the liability limit for power reactors from $1 billion to $1.2 billion and adjust the limits for lower-risk installations to reflect inflation; (2) establish a liability limit class for commercial small modular reactors (SMRs) recognizing their lower-risk profile; and (3) update provisions to designate the Darlington New Nuclear Project (DNNP) as a nuclear installation under the schedule to the Nuclear Liability and Compensation Regulations (NLCR), which will not come into force until a licence to operate is issued to the DNNP by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC).

records.title: Appointment of the High Commissioner for Canada in the Republic of Zambia.
records.summary: Appointment of Corry van Gaal as High Commissioner for Canada in the Republic of Zambia.

records.summary: Order (1) repealing P.C. 2018-49 of January 31, 2018; (2) designating the President of the King’s Privy Council for Canada, a member of the King’s Privy Council for Canada, as the Minister for the purposes of the Invest in Canada Act.

records.title: Canadian Ombudsperson for Responsible Enterprise
records.summary: Order repealing Order in Council P.C. 2019-299 of April 8, 2019, as amended by Order in Council P.C. 2019-1323 of September 6, 2019.

records.title: Acting Ministers Minute
records.summary: Appointment of those Cabinet Ministers who may act for the Prime Minister if he is unable to do so, as well as Acting Ministers for all the statutory portfolios.

records.title: Appointment of the Interim Chief Executive Officer of the Parks Canada Agency
records.summary: Appointment of Andrew Campbell of Ottawa, Ontario, to be interim Chief Executive Officer of the Parks Canada Agency, to hold office during pleasure for a term of six months or until such time as a new Chief Executive Officer is appointed, whichever occurs first.

records.title: Appointment of the Commissioner of Revenue
records.summary: Appointment of Heather Evans of Toronto, Ontario, to be Commissioner of Revenue, to hold office during pleasure for a term of five years, effective July 13, 2026.

records.title: Appointment of the High Commissioner for Canada in the Independent State of Samoa
records.summary: Appointment of Keith Smith as High Commissioner for Canada in the Independent State of Samoa, with residence in Wellington.

records.title: Appointment of the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the Federated States of Micronesia
records.summary: Appointment of David Hartman as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the Federated States of Micronesia, with residence in Manila.

records.title: Appointment of a Senior Advisor, Global Affairs Canada and of the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the European Union, in Brussels
records.summary: Appointment of the Honourable Jonathan Wilkinson, P.C., of Ottawa, Ontarioto be Senior Advisor, Global Affairs Canada, effective June 22, 2026, and concurrently Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the European Union, in Brussels, effective June 23, 2026.

records.title: Appointment of the Foreign Influence Transparency Commissioner
records.statute: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act
records.summary: Appointment of Anton Boegman of Victoria, British Columbia, to be Foreign Influence Transparency Commissioner, to hold office during good behaviour for a term of seven years, effective august 4, 2026.

records.title: Funding to Renew Nature Programs
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of the Environnement, until March 31, 2031, to lease any lands, or purchase or acquire any lands or any interests or rights in any lands, in an amount that does not exceed $35,000,000.

records.title: Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, done at New York on June 19, 2023.

records.title: Appointment of a Deputy Commissioner - RCMP
records.summary: Order appointing Lisa Diana Moreland of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police to the rank of Deputy Commissioner .

records.title: Order Designating Daniel Ross Morrow - Commanding Officer of “H” Division for the province of Nova Scotia
records.summary: Order designating Daniel Ross Morrow of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police as Commanding Officer of “H” Division for the province of Nova Scotia.

records.title: Order Designating Robin Emmanuel McNeil - Commanding Officer of “F” Division for the province of Saskatchewan
records.summary: Order designating Robin Emmanuel McNeil of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police as Commanding Officer of “F” Division for the province of Saskatchewan.

records.title: Order Appointing Official Receivers
records.summary: Order appointing seven (7) officers of the Office of the Superintendent of Bankruptcy of the Department of Innovation, Science and Economic Development as Official Receivers.

records.title: Official Receivers ** Termination**
records.summary: Order terminating the appointment of five (5) officers of the Office of the Superintendent of Bankruptcy of the Department of Industry as Officials Receivers.

records.title: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 301, British Columbia
records.summary: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 301 in order to (1) declare the natural disaster to be of concern to the federal government; and (2) authorize the provision of financial assistance to British Columbia with respect to the rainstorm that occurred in British Columbia, in December 2025.

records.title: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 299, Manitoba
records.summary: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 299 in order to (1) declare the natural disaster to be of concern to the federal government; and (2) authorize the provision of financial assistance to Manitoba with respect to the interface fires that occurred in Manitoba, from April to August 2025.

records.title: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 298, Manitoba
records.summary: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 298 in order to (1) declare the natural disaster to be of concern to the federal government; and (2) authorize the provision of financial assistance to Manitoba with respect to the interface fires that occurred in Manitoba, from May to September 2025.

records.title: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 291, Saskatchewan
records.summary: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 291 in order to (1) declare the natural disaster to be of concern to the federal government; and (2) authorize the provision of financial assistance to Saskatchewan with respect to the interface fires that occurred in Saskatchewan, from May to August 2025.

records.title: Order Approving the Collective Agreement between the Canadian Security Intelligence Service and the Public Service Alliance of Canada
records.statute: Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act
records.summary: Order authorizing the Canadian Security Intelligence Service to enter into a collective agreement with the Public Service Alliance of Canada for the period beginning on April 1, 2021 and ending on March 31, 2025.

records.title: Order Authorizing the Canada Lands Company Limited to incorporate new subsidiary
records.summary: Order Authorizing the Canada Lands Company Limited (CLCL) to incorporate new subsidiary in order to (1) procure the incorporation of a wholly- owned subsidiary that has yet to be named to carry out activities and perform functions in support of the mandate of CLCL, including with respect to the CN Tower, all the shares of which, on incorporation, would be held by, on behalf of or in trust for the CLCL; and (2) acquire shares of the wholly-owned subsidiary that, on acquisition, would be held by, on behalf of or in trust for CLCL.

records.title: Agreement between the European Union and Canada laying down the conditions for the participation of Canadian legal entities and products originating in Canada to procurement under the SAFE Instrument
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Agreement between the European Union and Canada laying down the conditions for the participation of Canadian legal entities and products originating in Canada to procurement under the SAFE Instrument done at Munich on 14 February, 2026.

records.title: Agreement between Canada and Australia on Cooperation and Mutual Administrative Assistance in Customs Matters
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Agreement between Canada and Australia on Cooperation and Mutual Administrative Assistance in Customs Matters, done at Wellington on 19 November 2025.

records.title: Order approving that the Minister of the Environment enter into the environmental occurrences notification agreements with the governments of Ontario, Manitoba, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Alberta and Yukon
records.summary: Order approving that the Minister of the Environment enter into the environmental occurrences notification agreements with the governments of Ontario, Manitoba, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Alberta and Yukon.

records.title: Order Fixing the Day on Which this Order Is Made as the Day on Which Division 2 of Part 5 of the Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 Comes into Force
records.summary: Order fixing the day on which this order is made as the day on which division 2 of part 5 of the Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 comes into force in order to modify the Canada Post Corporation Act that empower Canada Post Corporation to adjust stamp rates without Governor In Council regulatory approval, while retaining the legislative criteria requiring that rates remain fair and reasonable and consistent so far as possible with providing a revenue, together with any revenue from other sources, sufficient to defray operational costs.

records.title: Protocol on the Accession of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Protocol on the Accession of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, as well as any accompanying legally binding instruments.

records.title: Order Fixing the Date of the Coming into Force of the Act to implement the Protocol on the Accession of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
records.statute: An Act to implement the Protocol on the Accession of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
records.summary: Order fixing the date of the coming into force of An Act to implement the Protocol on the Accession of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership as the day on which the Protocol enters into force.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Canadian International Trade Tribunal Procurement Inquiry Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Canadian International Trade Tribunal Procurement Inquiry Regulations in order to add the United Kingdom as a Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership Member to Part 10 of the Schedule.

records.title: Order Amending the Import Control List (2026-2)
records.summary: Order Amending the Import Control List (2026-2) in order to remove references to the UK as ‘exempt’ from import permit requirements.

records.title: Order Amending the Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Order
records.summary: Order Amending the Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Order in order to (1) extend the exemption provided for steel derivative goods used in the manufacturing of motor vehicles, aerospace goods, and their parts to June 30, 2027; and (2) exempt goods originating in Canada from the surtax.

records.title: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025)
records.summary: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025) in order to (1) extend remission to (i) 293 products which remits surtaxes to any importer in respect of products that have been determined to be in short supply; (ii) 4 products which remits surtaxes to any importer in respect of products imported from the United States (U.S.) on a time-limited basis; (iii) 235 products which remit surtaxes for certain products imported from the U.S. due to exceptional circumstances that could have significant adverse impacts on the Canadian economy, such as preexisting contractual obligations; (iv) 179 products to remit surtaxes to any importer in respect of steel mill products that have been determined not to be produced in Canada; and (2) extend relief for (i) public health, health care, public safety and national security purposes until June 30, 2027; (ii) manufacturing, processing, food and beverage packaging or agricultural production until June 30, 2027; (iii) the manufacturing of motor vehicles, aerospace goods, and their parts until June 30, 2027.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations in order to (1) increase the current portfolio loan limit from $34 billion to $40 billion; and (2) restrict the eligibility of the full-time grant to students attending public institutions and not-for-profit private institutions in Canada, with exemptions.

records.title: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Regulations
records.statute: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act
records.summary: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Regulations in order to (1) identify the information that must be provided to the Commissioner by a person who enters into an arrangement with a foreign principal, including information on the person, the foreign principal and the nature and scope of the agreement; (2) establish the information displayed in the public-facing registry required under the act; (3) allow for the disclosure of information to specific federal partners, as well as provincial, territorial, and municipal bodies responsible for elections, lobbying, or conflict of interest matters; and (4) establish components of an administrative monetary penalties regime, including the range of penalty amounts, the criteria the Commissioner would consider in determining the penalty amount, the manner in which a notice of violation can be issued, and the ability to enter into compliance agreements.

records.title: Order Fixing August 4, 2026 as the Day on Which Part 4 of the Countering Foreign Interference Act, Other than Certain Provisions of the Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act, Comes into Force
records.summary: Order fixing August 4, 2026 as the day on which Part 4 of the Countering Foreign Interference Act, other than certain provisions of the Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act, comes into force in order to increase transparency around foreign influence activities, deterring malign foreign interference, and strengthening national security.

records.title: Regulations Amending and Repealing Certain Regulations Made Under the Export and Import Permits Act (Miscellaneous Program)
records.summary: Regulations Amending and Repealing Certain Regulations Made Under the Export and Import Permits Act (Miscellaneous Program) in order to (1) repeal two regulations that no longer have any practical application; (2) remove two items from the Export Control List for which export permits are no longer required; and (3) make minor technical, non-consequential amendments to increase clarity and reduce potential for confusion amongst stakeholders.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Superannuation Regulations and the Former Members of Parliament Counting of Service Regulations
records.statute: Royal Canadian Mounted Police Superannuation Act
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Superannuation Regulations and the Former Members of Parliament Counting of Service Regulations in order to (1) add provisions to prescribe that a member on leave to work as a full-time paid official of a bargaining agent must pay, by lump sum, double the employee share of contributions in advance of each quarter or year of their period of leave; and (2) add the interest rate and the manner to elect prior service as a member of Parliament as pensionable under the Pension Plan.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Transit Between International Flights)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Transit Between International Flights) in order to (1) create a definition for a designated holding area that mirrors the definition in the Presentation of Persons (2003) Regulations (POPR) and Reporting of Imported Goods Regulations (RIGR); (2) specify that international transiting travellers who remain in a sterile transit area or a designated holding area will be making an application to transit through Canada and not seeking to enter the country; (3) require that a person who leaves a sterile transit area (other than to enter a designated holding area) or who leaves a designated holding area (other than to enter a sterile transit area) present themselves for examination; and (4) require that commercial air carriers provide the Canada Border Services Agency with additional information on all passengers and crew as part of their Advance Passenger Information submission, which includes information about whether each person is seeking to enter Canada or is transiting through Canada on a flight bound for Canada, if they are transiting through Canada, their first destination outside Canada.

records.title: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Customs Act (Transit Between International Flights)
records.summary: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Customs Act (Transit Between International Flights) in order to (1) update the definition of a designated holding area to highlight that it is an area that is physically separated from other areas; (2) require that commercial air carriers provide the Canada Border Services Agency with additional information as part of their Advance Passenger Information submission (including the status of every person on board a flight bound for Canada or information about their first destination outside Canada if they are transiting through Canada); and (3) require that commercial air carriers provide the first destination outside of Canada of the persons or goods on board the aircraft, and the date and time of their arrival, as part of their Air Exit Information submission.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Privacy Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Privacy Regulations in order to (1) add three directorates to Schedule II as investigative bodies: (i) Environmental Enforcement Directorate, Department of the Environment; (ii) Wildlife Enforcement Directorate, Department of the Environment; and (iii) High Net Worth Compliance Directorate, Compliance Programs Branch, Canada Revenue Agency; and (2) remove the reference to the Security Intelligence Review Committee from the list in Schedule II.

records.title: Honda Canada Inc. Remission Order
records.summary: Honda Canada Inc. Remission Order in order to provide remission of customs duties paid by Honda Canada of $493,106 for imports of motor vehicles from the United States between June 7 to July 7, 2020.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Sulphur in Gasoline Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Sulphur in Gasoline Regulations in order to (1) re-enact the temporary sulphur compliance unit (SCU) trading system for the years 2026 to 2030; and (2) enable regulated parties to transfer the surplus balances of SCUs that they generated or received in trade in the expired trading system and owned as of March 31, 2026, into the re-enacted temporary trading system.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Authorizations Concerning Fish and Fish Habitat Protection Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Authorizations Concerning Fish and Fish Habitat Protection Regulations in order to (1) adjust the wording of certain standard information requirements in Schedule 1 to increase flexibility for the submission of slightly less detailed information for lower impact projects; (2) add the requirement to provide an email address and the requirement to provide date-stamped photographs that clearly indicate the habitat characteristics that are likely to be affected by the proposed work, undertaking or activity; (3) remove the requirement to provide contingency measures if the planned avoidance and mitigation measures and offsetting measures do not meet their objective, and make it optional to provide an estimate of the abundance of the fish species present; (4) add that information on physical works must include the area, in square metres, of fish habitat expected to be affected, while clarifying that project engineering specifications, scale drawings, and dimensional drawings only need to be provided for works in or near water; and (5) modify the information to be submitted about any engagement activities undertaken to harmonize with Indigenous engagement information requirement of the Information and Management of Time Limits Regulations.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Fishery (General) Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Fishery (General) Regulations in order to (1) add 57 major fish stocks to Schedule IX of the Regulations; (2) correct geographic descriptions of three prescribed stocks; and (3) reorder the list of stocks alphabetically.

records.title: Order Repealing the Railway Employee Qualification Standards Regulations
records.summary: Order Repealing the Railway Employee Qualification Standards Regulations in order to replace them with the Railway Personnel Training and Qualifications Regulations.

records.title: Railway Personnel Training and Qualifications Regulations
records.statute: Railway Safety Act Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act
records.summary: Railway Personnel Training and Qualifications Regulations in order to (1) add two new positions critical to safe railway operations; (2) add a requirement for railway companies to ensure employees with less than two years of experience in a position critical to safe railway operations are able to have contact with employees who have more than two years of relevant experience; (3) establish new types of training such as continuing training and familiarization training; (4) integrate Crew Resource Management into training; and (5) add a requirement to have a training record for each person who takes the training and undergoes the examinations and evaluations required under the regulations.

records.title: Order Amending the Certain Russian Goods Remission Order
records.summary: Order Amending the Certain Russian Goods Remission Order in order to provide duty relief for imports of titanium used in landing gear for airplanes of tariff item 8807.20.00.00 originating in Russia entering Canada between March 22, 2022, until April 16, 2029.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations in order to extend the current (2025-2026) funding levels of grants and loans for the 2026-2027 academic year.

records.title: Certain Canned Vegetable Goods Surtax Order
records.summary: Certain Canned Vegetable Goods Surtax Order in order to impose a 10% surtax for up to 200 days on imports from all countries, except imports from certain free trade partners (the United States, Mexico, Chile, Israel, and other Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement beneficiaries) and developing countries.

records.title: Order Terminating the Assignment of the Honourable Nathalie Provost and Assigning the Honourable Nathalie Provost to Assist the Minister of the Environment, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and the Minister of Natural Resources
records.statute: Ministries and Ministers of State Act
records.summary: Order terminating the Assignment of the Honourable Nathalie Provost made by Order in Council P.C. 2025-478 of May 13, 2025; and assigns the Honourable Nathalie Provost, Minister of State (Nature) to be styled Secretary of State (Nature), to assist the Minister of the Environment, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and the Minister of Natural Resources in the carrying out of those Ministers’ responsibilities.

records.summary: Order directing that a warrant be prepared authorizing the expenditure of sums set forth in Appropriation Act, No. 3, 2026-27. [Release of supply for Supplementary Estimates (A) for 2026-27]

records.title: Release of Full Supply for Main Estimates - 2026-27 ** Warrant **
records.summary: Order directing that a warrant be prepared authorizing the expenditure of sums set out in the Appropriation Act No. 2, 2026-27. [Release of full supply for the main estimates - 2026-27]

records.title: Appointment of the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the Republic of Ecuador
records.summary: Appointment of Mazen Mahfouz as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the Republic of Ecuador.

records.title: Residency exemption within the Canada Industrial Relations Board
records.summary: Order exempting two Governor in Council appointees of the Canada Industrial Relations Board from the National Capital Region residency requirement set out in section 10.1 of the Canada Labour Code.

records.title: Order fixing the acting pay (Various Governor in Council positions)
records.summary: Order fixing the acting pay for various Governor in Council positions.

records.title: Salary Order (Heads of Agencies)
records.summary: Salary Order (Heads of Agencies)

records.title: Order fixing the remuneration of the Special Assistant at the Prime Minister's official residence.
records.summary: Order fixing the remuneration of Daniela Visean, Special Assistant at the Prime Minister's official residence, effective May 11, 2026.

records.title: Order fixing the remuneration of the Secretary of the Treasury Board
records.summary: Order fixing the remuneration of William Matthews, Secretary of the Treasury Board, effective April 1, 2026.

records.title: Appointment of a director of the St. John’s Port Authority
records.summary: Appointment of Mark G. Duggan of St. John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, to be a director of the St. John’s Port Authority, to hold office for a term of three years, in the place of Beth Maureen McGrath, whose term has expired.

records.title: Order Authorizing the Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of Republic of Ecuador Concerning the Free Trade Agreement
records.summary: Order authorizing (1) the Prime Minister or the Minister of Foreign Affairs to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Free Trade Agreement between Canada and the Republic of Ecuador; or (2) the Minister of Foreign Affairs to execute and issue an Instrument of Full Powers, authorizing the individuals mentioned in the order, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Agreement.

records.title: Inter-American Convention on the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women (Convention of Belém do Pará)
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to ratify, on behalf of Canada, the Inter-American Convention on the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women (“Convention of Belém do Pará”), done at Belém do Pará on June 9, 1994.

records.title: Order Directing that a Proclamation be issued Designating Fire Prevention Week - October 4 to 10, 2026
records.summary: Order directing that a Proclamation be issued designating the week October 4 to 10, 2026, as Fire Prevention Week.

records.title: Order authorizing the leave of absence of the Honourable Ritu Khullar
records.summary: Order approving a leave of absence to the Honourable Ritu Khullar, Chief Justice of the Court of Appeal of Alberta, from her judicial duties from July 13, 2026, until January 12, 2027.

records.title: Order Appointing Ernst & Young LLP and the Auditor General of Canada as Joint Auditors of the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation
records.statute: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation Act Financial Administration Act
records.summary: Order appointing Ernst & Young LLP of Ottawa, Ontario and the Auditor General of Canada as joint auditors of the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation for the year 2026.

records.title: Order declining to vary, rescind or refer back to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission for reconsideration
records.summary: Order declining to vary, rescind or refer back to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) for reconsideration Telcom Decision CRTC 2025-157- Iristel Inc., thereby letting it stand.

records.title: Regulations Amending the New Harmonized Value-added Tax System Regulations, No. 2 (Ontario)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the New Harmonized Value-added Tax System Regulations, No. 2 (Ontario) in order to (1) implement temporary enhancements to the existing Ontario Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) New Housing Rebate and Ontario New Residential Rental Property Rebate for qualifying new housing in Ontario based on the province’s eligibility criteria; and (2) provide relief of the full 8% provincial portion of the HST on qualifying new homes.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Old Age Security Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Old Age Security Regulations (Miscellaneous Program) in order to introduces amendments which will allow for payments under the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), allowance for the Survivor top-up provisions to be rounded in the same way as the Old Age Security (OAS) pension and GIS, i.e., rounding down if the third decimal is 4 or less and rounding up if it is 5 or more.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Seizure and Facilities for Holding and Examination —Miscellaneous Program)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Seizure and Facilities for Holding and Examination —Miscellaneous Program) in order to (1) specify that an applicant seeking to have a seized thing returned must “make written submissions” rather than “demonstrate” that the seizure of the thing is no longer needed for the prevention of improper or fraudulent use; (2) specify that once a decision has been made to return the thing that it “must” rather than “shall” be returned without delay; and (3) clarify provisions regarding the provision of facilities for holding and examination by replacing the term” without cost to Her Majesty” with the term “free of charge” and better aligning the French version with the English version.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (Canadian Update)
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (Canadian Update) in order to (1) bring several modifications and updates to existing requirements and promote consistency, and uniform interpretation; (2) reduce the number of equivalency certificates (ECs) issued by Transport Canada under the authority of the Act by incorporating new regulatory provisions that cover activities currently permitted through ECs; (3) update existing requirements for rail transportation to better align the Canadian buffer car rules with the US regulations; and (4) harmonize the regulations with the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015, regarding the transportation of radioactive materials of unknown classification back to the consignors for characterization.

records.title: Collective Agreement between the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions of Canada and Public Service Alliance of Canada
records.statute: Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act
records.summary: Order authorizing the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions to enter into a collective agreement with the Public Service Alliance of Canada (PSAC) that covers all employees in the Administrative Support Group bargaining unit for the period beginning on April 1, 2023 and ending on March 31, 2025.

records.title: Canada-Indonesia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Canada-Indonesia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement done at Ottawa on 24 September 2025.

records.title: CICEPA Tariff Preference Regulations
records.summary: CICEPA Tariff Preference Regulations in order to allow eligible goods that are not shipped directly to Canada from Indonesia to retain their eligibility for preferential tariff rates provided the goods remain under customs control in third countries.

records.title: CICEPA Rules of Origin for Casual Goods Regulations
records.summary: CICEPA Rules of Origin for Casual Goods Regulations in order to establish that non-commercial goods acquired in Indonesia, that are either marked as made in Indonesia or not marked to the contrary, are considered originating and therefore entitled to the relevant CICEPA tariff preferences upon their importation into Canada.

records.title: CICEPA Rules of Origin Regulations
records.summary: CICEPA Rules of Origin Regulations in order to implement, in Canada, the rules of origin of the Agreement to determine when goods have undergone sufficient production to qualify for preferential tariff treatment.

records.title: Order Fixing the Day of Entry into Force of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement between Canada and Indonesia as the Day on Which the Canada–Indonesia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation Act Comes into Force
records.statute: Canada–Indonesia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation Act
records.summary: Order fixing the day of entry into force of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement between Canada and Indonesia (CEPA) as the day on which the Canada–Indonesia CEPA implementation act comes into force.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Canada Disability Benefit Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Canada Disability Benefit Regulations in order to (1) provide for a supplemental payment of $150 for each Disability Tax Credit certification or re-certification for program recipients; and 2) revise the definition of “adjusted income,” clarify the treatment of income for people who are granted a spousal/partner tax filing waiver, pause the accrual of interest on debts during reconsiderations, appeals and judicial reviews, and clarify the treatment of applications for people who are near their 18th birthday.

records.title: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of the Republic of Korea on the Protection of Military and Defence Classified Information, done at Ottawa on 25 February 2026.
records.summary: Order authorizing the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, or a delegate, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of the Republic of Korea on the Protection of Military and Defence Classified Information.

records.title: Treaty between Canada and Japan on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
records.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Treaty Between Canada and Japan on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters, done at Ottawa on 12 December 2025.

records.title: Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of Japan concerning the Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology

records.title: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations

records.title: Regulations Amending Certain Department of Health Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
records.statute: Food and Drugs Act Pest Control Products Act Assisted Human Reproduction Act Human Pathogens and Toxins Act Canada Consumer Product Safety Act Cannabis Act
records.summary: Regulations Amending Certain Department of Health Regulations (Miscellaneous Program) in order to (1) repeal obsolete or spent regulatory provisions that have no current application; (2) correct discrepancies between the French and English text of the regulations to improve clarity and reduce the risk of inconsistent interpretation; (3) correct discrepancies between the use of certain terms to increase consistency in interpretation; (4) harmonize terms with those used in related regulations to improve alignment and clarity; (5) improve the clarity of various provisions to facilitate consistent interpretation; and (6) update references to standards and other documents incorporated by reference (where the change is non-substantive).

records.title: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992 (Part 12 and International Harmonization Update)
records.summary: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992 (Part 12 and International Harmonization Update) in order to (1) incorporate changes and new requirements adopted under international codes and regulatory requirements; (2) amend dangerous goods marks, classification information, shipping names, and packaging requirements; (3) update Canadian standards that are incorporated by reference, to better align with the United Nations Model Regulations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods for the design, manufacture, and use of means of containment; (4) allow, under certain conditions, the transportation of dangerous goods in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling, placarding and documentation requirements prescribed under Title 49 of the United States Code of Federal Regulations to facilitate the transportation of dangerous goods between the United States and Canada; and (5) rewrite Part 12 of the Regulation to modernize air transportation requirements and update provisions for transport to remote locations and exemptions for medical, scientific, industrial, aerial and enforcement activities to reflect current domestic needs.

records.title: Order Exempting Certain Navigable Waters Located in Newfoundland and Labrador from the Application of Sections 22 and 23 of the Canadian Navigable Waters Act

records.title: Regulations Amending the Medical Devices Regulations (Establishment Licences)

records.statute: Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation Act
records.summary: Regulations Amending the Canada–Nova Scotia Offshore Area Petroleum Operations Framework Regulations in order to (1) repeal section 83, which sets the limit on the volume of gas that the Regulator may authorize to be vented at an installation to be no greater than 15,000 standard m3 per year; and (2) allow the Regulator to authorize venting above that threshold that is required for safety inspections in accordance with the CSA, 2001.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Area Petroleum Operations Framework Regulations

records.title: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Food and Drugs Act (Shortages and Discontinuation of Sale of Drugs and Medical Devices)
records.summary: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Food and Drugs Act (Shortages and Discontinuation of Sale of Drugs and Medical Devices) in order to (1) allow the Minister to expand the scope of drugs that would be subject to regulatory obligations related to shortages, such as reporting, to additional drugs or classes of drugs, including certain over-the-counter drugs; (2) allow the Minister to require information to be provided, in certain circumstances, about a shortage of any drug that could present a risk of injury to human health if in shortage rather than only those drugs in scope of shortage reporting; (3) allow the Minister to increase the supply of a drug available to address a shortage by extending the expiration date for the drug in certain circumstances; (4) improve the exceptional importation and sale frameworks for drugs and medical devices; (5) improve and expand the reporting of drug and medical device shortages and discontinuations; (6) update the Urgent Public Health Need framework to include drugs authorized in the United Kingdom; and (7) make minor non-substantive amendments to improve consistency of language between English and French versions of regulatory text and to align with current drafting language conventions.

records.title: Order Amending the Ukraine Goods Remission Order

records.title: Regulations Amending the New Harmonized Value-added Tax System Regulations, No. 2 and the Real Property (GST/HST) Regulations
records.summary: Regulations Amending the New Harmonized Value-added Tax System Regulations, No. 2 and the Real Property (GST/HST) Regulations in order to (1) implement a rebate in respect of the provincial component of the HST for new housing purchased by first-time home buyers in Ontario based on the eligibility criteria set out in the federal First-Time Home Buyers’ GST Rebate; (2) extend the application of the provincial Enhanced HST Rental Rebate in Ontario, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland and Labrador to ensure that universities, public colleges and school authorities can generally claim equivalent relief of the provincial HST in respect of new student housing projects in those provinces; and (3).correct a technical deficiency (a missing cross-reference) in the existing rules in respect of the provincial Enhanced HST Rental Rebate in New Brunswick.

records.title: Regulations Amending the Aquatic Invasive Species Regulations

records.title: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to Ebola Disease in Canada Order (Immigration Applications and Documents)

after.title: Remission Order for Certain Fees Under the Passport and Other Travel Document Services Fees Regulations
after.summary: Remission Order for Certain Fees Under the Passport and Other Travel Document Services Fees Regulations in order to remit actual and anticipated outstanding debts resulting from the non-collection of passport fee increases for the period beginning on April 1, 2023, and ending on March 31, 2025.

after.title: Consular Services Fees (Performance Standards) Remission Order
after.summary: Consular Services Fees (Performance Standards) Remission Order in order to remit certain fees paid or payable by clients in relation to their travel document (e.g. passports) application when the processing of the application goes beyond 30 days.

after.title: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Canada Labour Code
after.summary: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Canada Labour Code in order to (1) establish new regulatory requirements for exposure to engineered nanomaterials, thermal stress, non-solar ultraviolet radiation and radon; (2) provide an approach for situations where exposure threshold limits have not been established; (3) update references to incorporated standards; (4) harmonize record keeping requirements; (5) clarify air sampling requirements; and (6) make consequential amendments to the Administrative Monetary Penalties (Canada Labour Code) Regulations to ensure enforcement of health and safety provisions under Part IV of the Code.

after.title: Regulations Amending the Contraventions Regulations (Tobacco and Vaping Products Act)
after.summary: Regulations Amending the Contraventions Regulations (Tobacco and Vaping Products Act) in order to (1) increase the fine amounts for seven offenses already listed in the schedule of the Contraventions Regulation; and (2) update certain existing short-form descriptions for the contravention to ensure they remain accurate following amendments to the Act to include the notion of “vaping product.”

after.title: Regulations Amending the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
after.summary: Regulations Amending the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Regulations (Miscellaneous Program) in order to (1) update the list to remove 62 harbours from various provinces in Schedule I; (2) add three (3) harbours to various provinces in Schedule I; and (3) make the corrections to the name or location of five (5) harbours already in Schedule I.

after.title: Regulations Amending Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
after.summary: Regulations Amending Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Miscellaneous Program) in order to (1) correct a typographical error; (2) correct a discrepancy between English and French versions; and (3) clarify an apparent duplication of text.

after.title: Order Amending the China Surtax Remission Order (2024), No. 2
after.summary: Order Amending the China Surtax Remission Order (2024), No. 2 in order to (1) add 9 items to Schedule 1, which remits surtaxes to any importer in respect of goods that have been determined to be in short supply, and update several existing product descriptions to better reflect tariff classifications and technical specifications; (2) change two items from product-specific relief to company-specific relief, as a domestic source of supply has been identified; and (3) extend the duration of remission for products listed in Schedule 1 and for eligible importers under Schedule 2 from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2026.

after.title: Order authorizing the Minister of Finance to provide financial assistance to the Canada Post Corporation for the period beginning April 1, 2025 and ending on March 31, 2026
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Finance to provide financial assistance to the Canada Post Corporation for the period beginning April 1, 2025 and ending on March 31, 2026, to a maximum of $1.008 billion in order to enable it to meet its operating and income charges during this period.

after.title: Supplementary Estimates (C) 2025-26 ** Tabling **
after.summary: Order authorizing the tabling in the House of Commons of Supplementary Estimates (C) for the federal public administration for the fiscal year ending on March 31, 2026.

after.title: Order Authorizing the Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food to enter into an Agreement with Newfoundland and Labrador to provide federal contributions to assist dairy and livestock producers
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food to enter into an agreement with Newfoundland and Labrador to provide federal contributions of up to $2.4 million under the Agricultural Disaster Relief Program (AgriRecovery) to assist dairy and livestock producers with the extraordinary costs incurred as a result of drought during the summer of 2025.

after.summary: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Provincial Nominee Program) in order to (1) replace the criteria for membership in the Provincial Nominee Class, including the authority of a federal officer to substitute an assessment by the province or territory; and (2) establish that the nominating province or territory has the sole responsibility to assess the person's ability to establish in Canada and intent to reside in the nominating province or territory.

after.title: Order setting the annual borrowing limit for the 2026-27 fiscal year
after.summary: Order (1) authorizing the Minister of Finance to borrow money on behalf of the Government of Canada and conduct activities related to the borrowing of money as he considers appropriate; (2) specifying $683 billion as the aggregate principal amount of money that the Minister of Finance may borrow in the period beginning on April 1, 2026 and ending on March 31, 2027; (3) designating which officials within the Department of Finance and the Bank of Canada can sign and countersign security certificates; (4) authorizing the Minister of Finance to appoint fiscal agents and registrars, for example, for any foreign currency debt issued by Canada in the 2026-27 fiscal year; and (5) authorizing payments out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the management of the public debt.

after.title: Coming into Force of the Canada-Republic of Ecuador Agreement on Social Security
after.summary: Order declaring the entry into force of the Agreement on Social Security between Canada and the Republic of Ecuador.

after.title: Canada - Ukraine on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Customs Matters ** Agreement **
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Agreement between Canada and Ukraine on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Customs Matters.

after.title: Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the European Resilience from Space for Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Programme
after.summary: Order authorizing the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, or a delegate, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the European Resilience from Space for Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Programme.

after.title: the Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the ACCESS Programme
after.summary: Order authorizing the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, or a delegate, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the ACCESS Programme.

after.title: Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the FutureNAV Programme
after.summary: Order authorizing the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, or a delegate, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the FutureNAV Programme.

after.title: Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the Moonlight Programme
after.summary: Order authorizing the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, or a delegate, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation by the Government of Canada in the Moonlight Programme.

after.title: Canada Lands Company Limited ** leases for 2026-27 **
after.summary: Order (1) authorizing the Old Port of Montréal Corporation Inc. to enter into up to 30 leases in 2026-27, retain and use any associated proceeds if the leases are consistent with the last corporate plan of Canada Lands Company Limited, in respect of that period; and (2) authorizing Parc Downsview Park Inc. to enter into up to 39 leases in 2026-2027, and to retain and use any associated proceeds if the leases are consistent with the last corporate plan of Canada Lands Company Limited, in respect of that period.

after.title: Order in Council Canada — New Brunswick Immigration Agreement and Newfoundland and Labrador Immigration Agreement
after.statute: Department of Citizenship and Immigration Act Immigration and Refugee Protection Act
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration to enter into separate Amending Agreements with New Brunswick (NB) and Newfoundland and Labrador (NL) in order to align with the proposed Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Provincial Nominee Program).

after.title: Appointment of Auditor of the Canada Lands Company Limited and its subsidiaries
after.summary: Order appointing the Auditor General of Canada as the auditor of Canada Lands Company Limited and its subsidiaries, Canada Lands Company CLC Limited, Old Port of Montréal Corporation Inc. and Parc Downsview Park Inc. for the fiscal year ending on March 31, 2026.

after.title: Appointment of Auditor of the Jacques-Cartier and Champlain Bridges Inc.
after.summary: Order appointing the Auditor General of Canada as the auditor of the Jacques-Cartier and Champlain Bridges Inc. for the fiscal year ending on March 31, 2027.

after.title: Administration and Control of Reserve Land Pheasant Rump Nakota Indian Reserve No. 68 and 68B, Saskatchewan ** Transfer **
after.summary: Order consenting and authorizing the transfer of administration and control of lands in a Pheasant Rump Nakota Indian Reserve No. 68 and 68B, in Saskatchewan, for the purposes of constructing, operating and maintaining a provincial public highway and works for public utility.

after.title: Order Approving the Dissolution of the Chambre de commerce Mont-Saint-Bruno
after.summary: Order approving the dissolution of the Chambre de commerce Mont-Saint-Bruno, in Quebec.

after.title: Order Approving the Change of boundary of the Chambre de commerce et d'Industrie Vallée-du-Richelieu, in Quebec
after.summary: Order approving the application by the Chambre de commerce et d'Industrie Vallée-du-Richelieu, in Quebec, to change the boundaries of its district from Saint-Antoine-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Marc-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Denis-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Charles-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Mathieu-de-Beloeil, Beloeil, Mont-Saint-Hilaire, Sainte-Madeleine, Sainte-Marie-Madeleine, McMasterville, Otterburn Park, Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Saint-Mathias-sur-Richelieu, Carignan, Chambly, Richelieu, Marieville, Rougemont, Saint-Césaire, Sainte-Angèle-de-Monnoir, Saint-Paul-d’Abbotsford and Ange-Gardien to Saint-Antoine-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Marc-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Denis-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Charles-sur-Richelieu, Saint-Mathieu-de-Beloeil, Beloeil, Mont-Saint-Hilaire, Sainte-Madeleine, Sainte-Marie-Madeleine, McMasterville, Otterburn Park, Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Saint-Mathias-sur-Richelieu, Carignan, Chambly, Richelieu, Marieville, Rougemont, Saint-Césaire, Sainte-Angèle-de-Monnoir, Saint-Paul-d’Abbotsford, Ange-Gardien and Saint-Basile-le-Grand.

after.title: Order Approving the Name Change of the Chambre de commerce et d'Industrie Vallée-du-Richelieu
after.summary: Order approving the application of the Chambre de commerce et d'Industrie Vallée-du-Richelieu, in Quebec, to change its name to the "Chambre de commerce et d’industrie Vallée-du-Richelieu–Rouville".

after.title: Order approving the resignation and Annuity of Honourable Heather J. Williams, a judge of the Superior Court of Justice of Ontario
after.summary: Order accepting the resignation and granting an annuity to the Honourable Heather J. Williams, a judge of the Superior Court of Justice of Ontario.

after.title: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Afghanistan) Remission Order
after.summary: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Afghanistan) Remission Order in order to remit the fee that was not collected for certain Afghan nationals whose application for permanent residency was or will be approved under a temporary public policy.

after.title: Fees Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status and for the Processing of a Sponsoship Application for Family Classes (Sudan) Remission Order
after.summary: Fees Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status and for the Processing of a Sponsorship Application for Family Classes (Sudan) Remission Order in order to remit (1) the Right of Permanent Residence Fee that was not collected or will not be collected from foreign nationals who apply for permanent residence under the family class and are granted exemptions under a temporary public policy; and (2) the Sponsorship Application Fee that was not collected or that will not be collected from Canadian citizens and permanent residents who apply to sponsor foreign nationals who request exemptions under a temporary public policy.

after.title: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Certain Foreign Nationals) Remission Order
after.summary: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Certain Foreign Nationals) Remission Order in order to remit the fee that was waived for eligible principal applicants and their accompanying family members whose applications were approved under a temporary public policy.

after.title: Fees Paid or Payable for the Processing of an Application for Permanent Resident Status (Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations) Remission Order, No. 1
after.summary: Fees Paid or Payable for the Processing of an Application for Permanent Resident Status (Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations) Remission Order, No. 1 in order to remit outstanding debts resulting from the non-collection of the humanitarian and compassionate permanent residence application processing fees.

after.title: Fees Paid or Payable for the Processing of an Application for Permanent Resident Status (Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations) Remission Order, No. 2
after.summary: Fees Paid or Payable for the Processing of an Application for Permanent Resident Status (Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations) Remission Order, No. 2 in order to remit outstanding debts resulting from the non-collection for eligible principal applicants and their accompanying family members whose applications were found ineligible under a temporary public policy.

after.title: Adjustment of Certain Fees Under the Passport and Other Travel Document Services Fees Regulations Remission Order
after.summary: Adjustment of Certain Fees Under the Passport and Other Travel Document Services Fees Regulations Remission Order in order to (1) remit the actual and anticipated outstanding debts resulting from the non-collection of passport fee increases; (2) remit the debt for uncollected Passport Program fee increases resulting from the department of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada’s (IRCC) non-application of the adjustment formulas found in the previous version of the Passport and Other Travel Document Services Fees Regulations from April 1, 2025, to January 25, 2026; and (3) remit the debt for uncollected Passport Program fee increases resulting from IRCC’s non-application of indexation requirements under the Service Fees Act for three Passport Program fees from April 1, 2019, to March 30, 2027.

after.title: Regulations Amending the Employment Insurance Regulations
after.summary: Regulations Amending the Employment Insurance Regulations in order to extend the Pilot Project No. 24 by six months until October 10, 2026.

after.title: United States Surtax Remission Order (Motor Vehicles 2026)
after.summary: United States Surtax Remission Order (Motor Vehicles 2026) in order to renew the automotive remission framework for one year, allowing eligible automakers to import a set number of vehicles free of Canada’s counter-tariffs, provided they maintain production and investment in Canada.

after.title: Regulations Amending the Agricultural Marketing Programs Regulations (2026)
after.summary: Regulations Amending the Agricultural Marketing Programs Regulations (2026) in order to temporarily increase the Advance Payments Program (APP)’s interest-free limit such as the portion of advances that the Government pays the interest from $100,000 to $250,000 for all non-canola advances for the 2026 program year.

after.title: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Regulations
after.statute: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act
after.summary: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Regulations in order to set out the detailed requirements pertaining to the compensation fund, committees of the College, the Registrar and other operational details necessary to fully operationalize the intent of the College Act.

after.title: Regulations Repealing Certain Regulations Made Under the Softwood Lumber Products Export Charge Act, 2006 (Miscellaneous Program)
after.statute: Softwood Lumber Products Export Charge Act, 2006
after.summary: Regulations Repealing Certain Regulations Made Under the Softwood Lumber Products Export Charge Act, 2006 (Miscellaneous Program) in order to repeal the Three Regulations, whose provisions are no longer in application.

after.title: Order Amending the Treaty Land Entitlement (Saskatchewan) Remission Order
after.summary: Order Amending the Treaty Land Entitlement (Saskatchewan) Remission Order in order to remits the tax payable on land purchases made by certain Indian bands of Saskatchewan in settlement of treaty land entitlement claims pursuant to the terms of binding agreements entered into by the bands, the Government of Canada and the Government of Saskatchewan.

after.title: Order Consenting to the Amendments of the Anishinabek Nation Education Agreement
after.summary: Order consenting to the amendments of the Anishinabek Nation Education Agreement as set out in the Schedule, in order to enable Anishinabek Nation First Nations who have not yet joined the Education Agreement ("new joiners") to utilize community-based approval processes for ratification to be added as a Party to the Education Agreement post-Effective Date.

after.title: Order Approving the Entering into Agreements to amend the terms and conditions of the seven First Nations sales tax administration agreements (FNST Agreements)
after.summary: Order approving that the Minister of Finance, on behalf of the Government of Canada, enter into agreements to amend First Nations Sales Tax Administration Agreements with each of the seven First Nations.

after.title: Order Ratifying the Final Acts of the World Radiocommunication Conference of the International Telecommunication Union
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Final Acts of the World Radiocommunication Conference of the International Telecommunication Union, adopted at the World Radiocommunication Conference held in Dubai from 20 November to 15 December 2023.

after.title: Order Ratifying the Final Acts of the Agreement between Canada and the European Union Amending Annex B of the Agreement on Civil Aviation Safety between Canada and the European Community.
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Agreement between Canada and the European Union Amending Annex B of the Agreement on Civil Aviation Safety between Canada and the European Community, done at Washington on 12 June 2024.

after.title: Order Ratifying the Framework Agreement for International Collaboration on Research and Development of Generation IV Nuclear Energy Systems
after.summary: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to bring into force for Canada the Framework Agreement for International Collaboration on Research and Development of Generation IV Nuclear Energy Systems, done at Paris on 29 January 2025.

after.title: Order Amending the Surtax on Imports of Certain Steel Goods Remission Order, 2025
after.summary: Order Amending the Surtax on Imports of Certain Steel Goods Remission Order, 2025 in order to (1) provide remission of the 50 percent surtax for eighty-four (84) types of imported steel goods for which there are no identified domestically produced alternatives; and (2) provide remission of the surtax paid or payable for subject steel goods imported into Canada or in transit to Canada on or before December 26, 2025.

after.title: Order declining to vary, rescind or refer back to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission for reconsideration
after.summary: Order declining to vary, rescind or refer back to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) for reconsideration Telcom Decision CRTC 2025-154, thereby letting it stand.

after.title: Order Designating the Minister of Employment and Social Development, a member of the King’s Privy Council for Canada to be the Minister for the purposes of the Canadian Sustainable Jobs Act.
after.summary: Order (1) repealing P.C. 2024-851 of June 27, 2024; (2) designating the Minister of Employment and Social Development, a member of the King’s Privy Council for Canada to be the Minister for the purposes of the Canadian Sustainable Jobs Act.

after.title: Order Designating the Minister of Natural Resources, a member of the King’s Privy Council for Canada to be a specified Minister for the purposes of the Canadian Sustainable Jobs Act
after.summary: Order (1) repealing P.C. 2024-852 of June 27, 2024; (2) designating the Minister of Natural Resources, a member of the King’s Privy Council for Canada to be a specified Minister for the purposes of the Canadian Sustainable Jobs Act.

after.title: Order Transferring from the Department of Natural Resources to the Department of Employment and Social Development the Control and Supervision of the Sustainable Jobs Secretariat
after.statute: Public Service Rearrangement and Transfer of Duties Act
after.summary: Order Transferring from the Department of Natural Resources to the Department of Employment and Social Development the Control and Supervision of the Sustainable Jobs Secretariat, effective May 1, 2026.

after.title: Appointment of the Assistant Clerk of the King's Privy Council for Canada (Orders in Council).
after.summary: Appointment of Janna Rinaldi, of the City of Ottawa, in the Province of Ontario, to be Assistant Clerk of the King's Privy Council for Canada (Orders in Council).

after.title: Order Referring the Matter of the Importation of Certain Wood Goods to the Canadian International Trade Tribunal
after.summary: Order Referring the Matter of the Importation of Certain Wood Goods to the Canadian International Trade Tribunal in order to hold an inquiry to determine whether the import of the three identified classes of wood goods have increased in quantity to a point where they are causing serious injury or threat of serious injury to domestic producers of like or directly competitive goods.

after.title: Appointment of the Parliamentary Budget Officer
after.summary: Appointment of Annette Ryan of Ottawa, Ontario, to be Parliamentary Budget Officer, to hold office during good behaviour for a term of seven years, effective April 22, 2026.

after.title: Transfer of a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal
after.statute: Department of Employment and Social Development Act Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1
after.summary: Transfer of Jacques Bouchard of Blainville, Quebec, a part-time member of the Social Security Tribunal who may hear matters in the Employment Insurance Section, to become a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal, to hold office during pleasure for a term ending October 9, 2027.

after.title: Transfer of a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal
after.statute: Department of Employment and Social Development Act Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1
after.summary: Transfer of Charline Bourque of Québec, Quebec, a part-time member of the Social Security Tribunal who may hear matters in the Employment Insurance Section, to become a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal, to hold office during pleasure for a term ending March 6, 2027.

after.title: Transfer of a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal
after.statute: Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1 Department of Employment and Social Development Act
after.summary: Transfer of Paul William Dusome of Barrie, Ontario, a part-time member of the Social Security Tribunal who may hear matters in the Employment Insurance Section, to become a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal, to hold office during pleasure for a term ending December 14, 2027.

after.title: Transfer of a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal
after.statute: Department of Employment and Social Development Act Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1
after.summary: Transfer of Suzanne Louisa Graves of Toronto, Ontario, a part-time member of the Social Security Tribunal who may hear matters in the Employment Insurance Section, to become a part-time member of the Employment Insurance Board of Appeal, to hold office during pleasure for a term ending June 21 2027.
